name: Hiram
description: Town in Portage County, Ohio, where Joseph Smith lived at the John Johnson home in 1831 and 1832 and received many revelations.

name: Amherst
description: Town in Lorain County, Ohio, where a conference of elders met in January 1832.

name: Chariton
description: Former frontier town at the mouth of the Chariton River on the Missouri, where Joseph Smith met elders bound for Zion in August 1831.
source: approximate, old town site near the Chariton River mouth about three miles above Glasgow, Missouri

name: Fishing River
description: River in Clay County, Missouri, where Zion's Camp camped in June 1834 after a storm scattered its enemies.
source: approximate, Zion's Camp site 2.8 miles southwest of Excelsior Springs (Ensign Peak Foundation)

name: Liberty Jail
description: The jail at Liberty, Missouri, where Joseph Smith and other church leaders were imprisoned in the winter of 1838 and 1839.

name: Ramus
description: Town in Hancock County, Illinois, southeast of Nauvoo, settled by the Saints in 1840 and later called Macedonia and Webster.

name: Winter Quarters
description: The settlement on the west bank of the Missouri River, in present Omaha, Nebraska, where the Saints wintered in 1846 and 1847.
source: Winter Quarters historical marker, 30th and Mormon Streets, Omaha (HMdb)

name: Salt Lake City
description: City in the Salt Lake Valley, Utah, founded by the pioneers in 1847 as the gathering place and headquarters of the church.
